tests.expected: Existing agent/configuration files are preserved until explicitly approved; no repository code executes during discovery.
Wrong signature/identity, expired trusted metadata when required, or artifact digest mismatch fails installation without privilege escalation.
An adapter missing required permission or cancellation semantics cannot silently enter a mode promising those capabilities.
Malformed, duplicated, and reordered events produce bounded errors or deduplicated updates, not duplicated runs or fabricated state.
Closing the supported client leaves supervisor-owned sessions running and attachable.
Reconciliation marks lost execution accurately; no unsupported promise of process restoration.
Cancellation reports pending/failed termination accurately and distinguishes it from external-action reversal.
Retries, new sessions, and provider swaps do not reset the approved task budget; usage remains observed/estimated/unknown.
Bounded buffers and quotas prevent controller memory exhaustion; required lost/truncated evidence prevents unsupported acceptance.
Concurrent edits cannot contaminate a fixed verification snapshot or receive its acceptance automatically.
Untracked files, symlinks, submodules, missing LFS content, and unsupported source states are explicitly handled or rejected.
Parallel tasks do not accidentally share allocated ports, writable database namespaces, or browser profiles.
Cycles are rejected; dependent work cannot consume an unspecified or unapproved predecessor artifact.
Agent edits to requirements, permissions, or required checks cannot silently alter the approved TaskContract.
A duplicated webhook or schedule occurrence does not create duplicate admitted work for the same trigger identity.
Unauthorized project content cannot leak through search, summaries, context caches, memory, or evidence views.
Untrusted issue/tool/browser content cannot authorize a tool, credential, policy change, or external transfer.
A restricted candidate cannot read controller keys, publish authoritative evidence, or use merge/deploy credentials.
If the required isolation backend is unavailable, execution is refused rather than downgraded to unrestricted local commands.
Changing candidate, action parameters, contract, or relevant policy invalidates the corresponding approval as specified.
Zero expected tests, missing required tools, malformed reports, and required checks not run never count as successful verification.
A generic zero exit code is not labeled as tests/security/compatibility passed without the applicable structured interpretation.
A cached or imported report for another snapshot/environment is not accepted for the current investigation.
Import/build/setup failure on base does not count as reproducing the target defect.
Failed attempts remain visible; acceptance follows an explicit approved retry/flakiness rule rather than cherry-picking a pass.
A passed formal tool cannot label excluded code, unsupported concurrency, unchecked axioms, or unbound requirements as proved.
An accidentally empty plan is inconclusive; explicit no-runtime-check profiles require their own approved acceptance conditions.
A lost response after PR creation/push triggers reconciliation, not an automatic duplicate side effect.
An obsolete ownership generation cannot publish authoritative completion or perform controller-mediated writes.
Passing individual branches does not waive verification of the actual integration/merge candidate.
An untrusted actor or skipped/neutral path cannot masquerade as the required successful Rover acceptance result.
Expired/deleted evidence remains identified as unavailable; the UI does not claim reproducibility from absent inputs.
Interrupted migration/update has a tested recovery path; restoring an old executable alone is not assumed sufficient.
A proposed strategy cannot remove mandatory checks, alter truth semantics, access evaluator secrets, or promote itself.
Merge/no-report/temporal-proximity signals are not silently converted into correctness or confirmed causal defect labels.
Training, tuning, and holdout access are tracked; private repository data does not enter shared learning without authorization.
Path traversal, symlink escape, oversized reports, and malicious terminal escape sequences cannot compromise extraction/rendering.
Candidate-controlled cache outputs cannot certify another build; reuse is denied when relevant mutable inputs are unaccounted for.
Database, infrastructure, and deployment operations require scoped approval and explicit recovery/compensation behavior.
User-owned code and Git history remain usable; export marks unsupported session portability and evidence omissions.
